attributes.docstring_full: Whether the fragment's LAST line must leave room for its bottom margin above the region's bottom edge: when it would not, that line goes on to the next page or column (a one-line fragment moves whole). The lines before it still fill the region to its edge - only the line the margin follows needs the margin's room. Off (the default) the last line may end on the edge and the margin runs past it.

attributes.docstring: Where a block background (BlockBackground) ENDS on the page a split paragraph leaves: this many em below its last baseline there, instead of at that line's box bottom.
attributes.docstring_full: Where a block background (BlockBackground) ENDS on the page a split paragraph leaves: this many em below its last baseline there, instead of at that line's box bottom. Zero (the default) keeps the line box. A caller whose typesetter closes a broken box at the face's descent (its leading below the line not painted) gives that descent here.

attributes.docstring: The fill opacity (ca) of the text alone, as a real in 0..1, used instead of the foreground colour's byte alpha when set.
attributes.docstring_full: The fill opacity ( ca ) of the text alone, as a real in 0..1, used instead of the foreground colour's byte alpha when set.

attributes.docstring: Indent applied to the first line of the paragraph (points).
Whether the space that separated a finished line from the word that overflowed it HANGS past the measure instead of being dropped.
attributes.docstring_full: Whether the space that separated a finished line from the word that overflowed it HANGS past the measure instead of being dropped. Both readings are right for their own typography, which is what makes this a policy rather than a defect. By default the wrap keeps that space only while it still fits, so a line never measures wider than its box. A hanging space is what CSS specifies for a soft wrap -- the space stays with the line and simply overhangs -- and a caller matching such a system asks for it here. It is a TEXT difference, not a visible one: the space renders past the margin where nothing shows.

attributes.docstring: Symbol used at line breaks when hyphenation is in effect (default "-").
Whether the paragraph's LAST line is stretched too (the way a "justify all" alignment does).
attributes.docstring_full: Whether the paragraph's LAST line is stretched too (the way a "justify all" alignment does). Off by default.

attributes.docstring: How a line aligned Justify is stretched to the measure: by character AND word spacing (Tc, Tw) rather than by moving its words.
attributes.docstring_full: How a line aligned Justify is stretched to the measure: by character AND word spacing ( Tc , Tw ) rather than by moving its words. The slack S of a line of n glyphs and s spaces is shared as Tw = r·B , Tc = (1−r)·B with B = S / ((1−r)(n−1) + r·s) : this value is r , the word share (1 = words only, 0 = glyphs only). Null (the default) keeps the flow's own justification. The last line is left as it is unless JustifyLastLine asks for it too.

attributes.docstring: Whether a line fits the region when its text reaches no lower than the region's bottom (or the room its paragraph keeps for its bottom margin): the half of the surplus leading below a line's descent may fall past it.
attributes.docstring_full: Whether a line fits the region when its text reaches no lower than the region's bottom (or the room its paragraph keeps for its bottom margin): the half of the surplus leading below a line's descent may fall past it. Off (the default) a line needs its whole line box. Lines of differing heights always need theirs.

attributes.docstring: The decimals each wrapped line's origin is written with: every line lands on its own origin rounded to them, halves away from zero, rather than one leading below the last.
attributes.docstring_full: The decimals each wrapped line's origin is written with: every line lands on its own origin rounded to them, halves away from zero, rather than one leading below the last. A caller whose own writer states positions to a fixed precision gives it here so the glyphs land where that writer's would. Null (the default) writes the origins as laid out. Rotated lines keep their exact origins.

attributes.docstring: Line-spacing interpretation mode.
attributes.docstring_full: Line-spacing interpretation mode. Default is FontSize.

attributes.docstring: Line-spacing value in points (internal extension — the public API exposes the mode only).
The most lines MinWidowLines may move over to the next page.

The fewest lines of the paragraph that may stand at the bottom of a page when it breaks there; with fewer room left the whole paragraph starts the next page, unless it already stands at the top of one.
attributes.docstring_full: The fewest lines of the paragraph that may stand at the bottom of a page when it breaks there; with fewer room left the whole paragraph starts the next page, unless it already stands at the top of one. 0 (the default) keeps any number.

attributes.docstring: The fewest lines of the paragraph that may be carried to the next page when it breaks; with fewer, lines are moved over to make them up - at most MaxWidowLinesMoved, and never so many that the lines left behind fall under MinOrphanLines (or one).
attributes.docstring_full: The fewest lines of the paragraph that may be carried to the next page when it breaks; with fewer, lines are moved over to make them up - at most MaxWidowLinesMoved, and never so many that the lines left behind fall under MinOrphanLines (or one). 0 (the default) carries any number.

attributes.docstring: When too few lines would be carried over and moving lines cannot make them up (MinWidowLines), the whole paragraph starts the next page instead of breaking as it would; off (the default), it breaks as it would.
The opacity of everything the fragment paints -- fill AND stroke, ca and CA of one graphics state -- as a real in 0..1.
attributes.docstring_full: The opacity of everything the fragment paints -- fill AND stroke, ca and CA of one graphics state -- as a real in 0..1. Null (the default) is opaque. A colour's own alpha is a byte; this keeps the exact value a caller gave.

attributes.docstring: A border around a RUN's box (a segment flowing as a run, see SegmentsFlowAsRuns): the box behind its text - its advance wide, its line box's ascent and descent tall - grown by the border's bands, painted as a block's border is (rounded with BackgroundCornerRadii), a background filling it out to the bands' outer edge.
attributes.docstring_full: A border around a RUN's box (a segment flowing as a run, see SegmentsFlowAsRuns): the box behind its text - its advance wide, its line box's ascent and descent tall - grown by the border's bands, painted as a block's border is (rounded with BackgroundCornerRadii), a background filling it out to the bands' outer edge. The run occupies both side bands and its text moves in by the left one; each line's piece is a whole bordered box. The line's height is the caller's: a caller whose leading follows the grown box states it in the run's line spacing. Null (the default) draws none.

attributes.docstring: For segments that flow as runs (SegmentsFlowAsRuns) in a declared line box: a line is this multiple of its HIGHEST ascent plus its DEEPEST descent tall, whichever runs reach them, and seats its baseline half the surplus under its top -- the rule of a typesetter whose leading multiplies the line's own extent, so runs in faces of different proportions box together.
attributes.docstring_full: For segments that flow as runs (SegmentsFlowAsRuns) in a declared line box: a line is this multiple of its HIGHEST ascent plus its DEEPEST descent tall, whichever runs reach them, and seats its baseline half the surplus under its top -- the rule of a typesetter whose leading multiplies the line's own extent, so runs in faces of different proportions box together. Unset, a line takes the tallest line box among its runs.

attributes.docstring: For segments that flow as runs: how far apart the default tab positions stand for a tab with no stop past it - the next multiple of this from where its line starts, and never past the line's end.
attributes.docstring_full: For segments that flow as runs: how far apart the default tab positions stand for a tab with no stop past it - the next multiple of this from where its line starts, and never past the line's end. Unset, every 36 points (half an inch).

attributes.docstring: For segments that flow as runs (SegmentsFlowAsRuns): the stops a tab segment (IsTab) goes to, measured from where each line starts.
attributes.docstring_full: For segments that flow as runs (SegmentsFlowAsRuns): the stops a tab segment (IsTab) goes to, measured from where each line starts. A tab reaches the first stop PAST where its line has got to. What follows a Left stop starts at it; what follows any other, up to the next tab or the line's end, is laid as though the tab took no room and then moved so that it ends at a Right stop, is centred on a Center one, or has its first AnchorCharacter on a Decimal one (ending there without it) - never moved back past the tab, and pulled back as far as it must be to end within the line. A stop past the line's width is still gone to; what follows then starts the next line.

attributes.docstring: Whether a caller-positioned fragment belongs to the page the FLOW HAS REACHED rather than the page it was added to.
attributes.docstring_full: Whether a caller-positioned fragment belongs to the page the FLOW HAS REACHED rather than the page it was added to. The two are the same until the flow moves on. After that they are different requests and only the caller knows which it means: content that names its page wants that page, and content that means "here, beside the text I have just added" wants wherever the flow now is. Without this the second lands on the flow's start page, stranded on page one while the text it belonged beside has moved. It does not consume flow space either way.

attributes.docstring: The fragment's segments flow as RUNS of one paragraph: the text wraps at spaces across them (a word split between two segments stays one word), every line is drawn run by run in each segment's own face, size and colour, and a line is as tall as the tallest line box among the runs on it, seated on the largest run's ascent -- a small run beside a large one shares the large one's baseline.
attributes.docstring_full: The fragment's segments flow as RUNS of one paragraph: the text wraps at spaces across them (a word split between two segments stays one word), every line is drawn run by run in each segment's own face, size and colour, and a line is as tall as the tallest line box among the runs on it, seated on the largest run's ascent -- a small run beside a large one shares the large one's baseline. Off by default: segments of differing styles then draw as one unwrapped line when they fit, and take the fixed-position writer when they do not.

A horizontal shear of the glyphs -- the text matrix's c component, the tangent of the angle the verticals lean by. Zero (the default) is upright. A shear is text state alone: the run advances by its glyphs, nothing else moves.

attributes.docstring: A vertical shear of the glyphs -- the text matrix's b component, the tangent of the angle the baseline climbs by along the run.
attributes.docstring_full: A vertical shear of the glyphs -- the text matrix's b component, the tangent of the angle the baseline climbs by along the run. Zero (the default) is level. Text state alone, like Skew.

attributes.docstring: The geometry of the strike-through drawn when IsStrikeOut is set; null (the default) keeps the flow's own rule.
Indent applied to lines after the first (points).

A synthetic weight: the glyphs are filled AND stroked with a pen this wide (2 Tr, w), the way a bold is simulated from a regular face, and the run OCCUPIES the pen's width more than its glyphs advance -- the stroke's overhang -- which the run after it, the wrap, the alignment and a rule under it all take in.
attributes.docstring_full: A synthetic weight: the glyphs are filled AND stroked with a pen this wide ( 2 Tr , w ), the way a bold is simulated from a regular face, and the run OCCUPIES the pen's width more than its glyphs advance -- the stroke's overhang -- which the run after it, the wrap, the alignment and a rule under it all take in. Zero (the default) is none. An explicit RenderingMode is text state alone and wins over this when set.

attributes.docstring: A synthetic slant: the glyphs are sheared by this tangent (added to Skew), the way an italic is simulated from an upright face, and the run OCCUPIES lean × size more than its glyphs advance -- the top of its em box leans that far past the last glyph -- which the run after it, the wrap and the alignment take in; a rule under it reaches half of it.
attributes.docstring_full: A synthetic slant: the glyphs are sheared by this tangent (added to Skew), the way an italic is simulated from an upright face, and the run OCCUPIES lean × size more than its glyphs advance -- the top of its em box leans that far past the last glyph -- which the run after it, the wrap and the alignment take in; a rule under it reaches half of it. Zero (the default) is none.

attributes.docstring: Creates options with WrapMode Undefined (wrap by width) and LineSpacing FontSize.
attributes.docstring_full: Creates options with WrapMode Undefined (wrap by width) and LineSpacing FontSize .

attributes.docstring: Whether the fragment's top margin is applied AGAIN where its lines continue on a new page or column.
attributes.docstring_full: Whether the fragment's top margin is applied AGAIN where its lines continue on a new page or column. Off (the default) the continuation starts flush at the region's top, the way a fragmented box does; a caller whose typesetter gives the continued part its own margin asks for it here. Each part then keeps its margins: the part left behind keeps the bottom margin under it, which a BoxBlock around the fragment closes under.

attributes.docstring: The paragraph's lines are not clipped to its band: a glyph that overhangs the measure (a serif's left bearing, a descender past the last line) is drawn whole, as a layout that never clips text draws it.
attributes.docstring_full: The paragraph's lines are not clipped to its band: a glyph that overhangs the measure (a serif's left bearing, a descender past the last line) is drawn whole, as a layout that never clips text draws it. Off, the band cuts what runs past it.

attributes.docstring: The geometry of the underline drawn when IsUnderline is set; null (the default) keeps the flow's own rule.
Gets or sets the word wrap mode for the paragraph.
attributes.docstring_full: Gets or sets the word wrap mode for the paragraph. Default is Undefined (the ctor sets the backing field to Undefined). The flow layout treats Undefined as "wrap by width" -- callers that want the no-wrap behaviour have to opt in explicitly.

attributes.docstring: Represents a fragment of text on a page with position and style information.
The text baseline position.
attributes.docstring_full: The text baseline position. Position includes descent offset (bottom of text rect); BaselinePosition is the actual text baseline (higher by |descent|).

attributes.docstring: Pictures painted over the block's background and under its border and text, the first on top (see BackgroundPicture).
attributes.docstring_full: Pictures painted over the block's background and under its border and text, the first on top (see BackgroundPicture). Empty (the default) paints none. Flow only.

attributes.docstring: A border drawn around the paragraph's BLOCK when it flows on a page: around its padding and line boxes, inside its Margin.
attributes.docstring_full: A border drawn around the paragraph's BLOCK when it flows on a page: around its padding and line boxes, inside its Margin. Each side is a band of its own width; the text starts inside the left band, wraps to the width that is left inside the left and right bands, and the block grows by the top and bottom bands. A BackgroundColor asked for as a block background covers the whole bordered box, bands included. Null (the default) draws none. Honoured by the flow only; a fragment placed at a position of its own ignores it.

attributes.docstring: Lays the fragment as a block box even when no other block property is set -- what makes the flow honour its Margin's LEFT and RIGHT, which a plain flow fragment has never taken.
attributes.docstring_full: Lays the fragment as a block box even when no other block property is set -- what makes the flow honour its Margin's LEFT and RIGHT, which a plain flow fragment has never taken. Off by default, so a caller who set a left margin years ago sees nothing move.

attributes.docstring: Rounds the block's corners (see CornerRadii): the background is painted inside the rounded outline and the BlockBorder inside the ring between it and the inner outline.
attributes.docstring_full: Rounds the block's corners (see CornerRadii): the background is painted inside the rounded outline and the BlockBorder inside the ring between it and the inner outline. A reach given as a fraction is of the bordered box's own width or height. Null (the default) leaves the corners square. Flow only.

attributes.docstring: Where a block narrower than its region stands across it.
attributes.docstring_full: Where a block narrower than its region stands across it. Left (the default) hugs the region's left edge; this is the BLOCK's place, not the alignment of the text inside it.

attributes.docstring: The most the block's content may be wide; the block shrinks to it when the region is wider.
attributes.docstring_full: The most the block's content may be wide; the block shrinks to it when the region is wider. Zero (the default) is no limit. Flow only.

attributes.docstring: The least the block's content box may be wide: a narrower declared or fitted width grows to it.
attributes.docstring_full: The least the block's content box may be wide: a narrower declared or fitted width grows to it. Zero (the default) is no floor. Flow only.

attributes.docstring: Space between the block's border (or its edge) and its line boxes, on each side.
attributes.docstring_full: Space between the block's border (or its edge) and its line boxes, on each side. Null (the default) is none. Flow only.

Where a SINGLE line stands inside a content box taller than it is. Top (the default) seats it at the top; Bottom puts its font descent flush with the box's bottom; Center halves that drop. Several lines always seat at the top.

attributes.docstring: The width of the block's CONTENT -- its line boxes -- in points; padding and border add outside it.
attributes.docstring_full: The width of the block's CONTENT -- its line boxes -- in points; padding and border add outside it. Zero (the default) takes the write region's width less the margins. A narrower block stands where BlockHorizontalAlignment puts it. Flow only.

attributes.docstring: The height of the block's content box, in points; padding and border add outside it.
attributes.docstring_full: The height of the block's content box, in points; padding and border add outside it. Lines that do not fit are DROPPED, and the flow continues under the box whatever its content took. Zero (the default) is the content's own height. Flow only.

attributes.docstring: The most the block's content box may be tall: a taller content is cut to it, lines beyond dropped, and a declared BoxHeight above it is brought down to it; the floor wins over it.
attributes.docstring_full: The most the block's content box may be tall: a taller content is cut to it, lines beyond dropped, and a declared BoxHeight above it is brought down to it; the floor wins over it. Zero (the default) is no cap.

attributes.docstring: The least the block's content box may be tall.
attributes.docstring_full: The least the block's content box may be tall. Zero (the default) is no floor. Flow only.

attributes.docstring: Shallow copy of the fragment (text + state).
attributes.docstring_full: Shallow copy of the fragment (text + state). Segments are regenerated from the cloned text.

attributes.docstring: Clone the fragment AND its segments.
attributes.docstring_full: Clone the fragment AND its segments. The cloned fragment has fresh segment instances that mirror the source's text+state.

attributes.docstring: Endnote attached to this fragment.
attributes.docstring_full: Endnote attached to this fragment. Stored only.

attributes.docstring: Shortcut for TextState.FontSize.
Optional footnote attached to this fragment.
attributes.docstring_full: Optional footnote attached to this fragment. Stored only; the layout engine does not currently render footnote references or the page-bottom note text.

attributes.docstring: The XForm this fragment was extracted from, or null for page-level fragments.
Horizontal alignment used when this fragment is laid out as a paragraph (added to page.Paragraphs).
attributes.docstring_full: Horizontal alignment used when this fragment is laid out as a paragraph (added to page.Paragraphs ). Stored on the fragment so callers can set alignment without touching TextState; the layout engine reads this on save.

attributes.docstring: Hyperlink applied to this fragment.
attributes.docstring_full: Hyperlink applied to this fragment. Set-only on the public surface; the underlying hyperlink action is wired into the page's annotation stream at save time (stored only in this build).

attributes.docstring: Legacy string-typed hyperlink target.
Force the paragraph to start a new column.
When true, this text fragment renders on the same line as the previous in-line paragraph.
attributes.docstring_full: When true, this text fragment renders on the same line as the previous in-line paragraph. Currently a state flag — layout wiring follows once Image / inline-flow rendering is implemented.

attributes.docstring: Whether the fragment's lines stay on ONE page: when they do not all fit in the room left on the current page but would fit an empty one, the fragment starts on the next page instead of splitting.
attributes.docstring_full: Whether the fragment's lines stay on ONE page: when they do not all fit in the room left on the current page but would fit an empty one, the fragment starts on the next page instead of splitting. One taller than a page splits anyway. Flow only.

attributes.docstring: Keep this paragraph on the same page as the next one.

Isolate the character range [startIndex, startIndex+length) (startIndex is a 0-based character offset into the fragment's text) into its own TextSegment(s): the covering segment is split into up to three pieces (before / isolated / after), each inheriting the original segment's TextState, and the fragment's Segments collection is rebuilt to reflect the split.
attributes.docstring_full: Isolate the character range [startIndex, startIndex+length) (startIndex is a 0-based character offset into the fragment's text) into its own TextSegment(s): the covering segment is split into up to three pieces (before / isolated / after), each inheriting the original segment's TextState, and the fragment's Segments collection is rebuilt to reflect the split. Returns the isolated (middle) segments so a caller can restyle just that range, e.g. recolour "95" inside "Windows 95 ".

attributes.docstring: Margin information for layout when used as a paragraph element.
The page this fragment belongs to (public alias for SourcePage).
The page index (0-based) this fragment was found on.
The text position.
The bounding rectangle of this text fragment on the page.
Text-replacement options used by TextFragmentAbsorber replace paths.
attributes.docstring_full: Text-replacement options used by TextFragmentAbsorber replace paths. Lazy-initialised on first access so callers can mutate properties without setting a fresh instance first.

attributes.docstring: The collection of text segments that make up this fragment (1-indexed).
attributes.docstring_full: The collection of text segments that make up this fragment (1-indexed). A newly constructed fragment always contains at least one segment. Setter replaces every segment with the supplied collection's items.

attributes.docstring: Tab stops for this fragment (used with #$TAB markers in text).
The text content.
attributes.docstring_full: The text content. Setting this property replaces the text in the PDF content stream when a source page reference is available (i.e. when the fragment was obtained from a TextFragmentAbsorber).

attributes.docstring: Edit options applied during text replacement / font substitution.
Create an empty text fragment.
Text state (font, size, color).
attributes.docstring_full: Text state (font, size, color). Fragment-typed wrapper around the underlying TextState so callers can reach Font as Font and the fragment-only members (DrawTextRectangleBorder, TabStops, IsFitRectangle).

attributes.docstring: Number of wrapped lines computed during layout.
attributes.docstring_full: Number of wrapped lines computed during layout. 0 until layout runs.

attributes.docstring: Z-order of the paragraph on its page: a page's paragraphs are laid out and painted in ascending order (added order among equals), so a higher index draws on top.
Searches for text fragments on PDF pages, optionally matching a search phrase.
Apply the supplied font to every absorbed fragment.
Diagnostics emitted while extracting text.
attributes.docstring_full: Diagnostics emitted while extracting text. Empty unless extraction reports an error.

attributes.docstring: Gets or sets the text extraction options.
True when Errors has at least one entry.
Gets or sets the search phrase.
attributes.docstring_full: Gets or sets the search phrase. Setting clears previous results.

attributes.docstring: Per-regex fragment groups when constructed via the Regex[] ctor; empty otherwise.
Replace every fragment's text with the empty string across every page in the document.
Clear absorbed fragments, errors, and per-regex results.
Gets the concatenated text of all found fragments.
Edit options applied during text replacement / font substitution.
Create an absorber that collects all text fragments.
Found text fragments.
attributes.docstring_full: Found text fragments. 1-based indexer matching the public API.

attributes.docstring: Gets or sets text replace options for controlling replacement behavior.
attributes.docstring_full: Gets or sets text replace options for controlling replacement behavior. The absorber's default action is ShiftRestOfLine: replacing a match with shorter/longer text shifts the rest of the line by the width delta. Callers opt OUT of the shift by setting ReplaceAdjustment.None explicitly.

attributes.docstring: Gets or sets the text search options.
attributes.docstring_full: Gets or sets the text search options. Can be set after construction to configure rectangle-bounded search and other options.

attributes.docstring: Visit a page and extract/search text fragments.
A 1-indexed collection of TextFragment objects, matching the public API.
Adds a fragment to the end of the collection; throws when fragment is null.
attributes.docstring_full: Adds a fragment to the end of the collection; throws when fragment is null .

attributes.docstring: Append every fragment from fragments to this collection.
Clear all fragments from the collection.
Returns true when the collection contains the given fragment.
Copies the fragments into array, starting at the zero-based index.
attributes.docstring_full: Copies the fragments into array , starting at the zero-based index .

attributes.docstring: Number of fragments.
Removes the given fragment and deletes its text from the page content it was absorbed from; returns true when it was found.
Creates an empty fragment collection.
Fragment-level text formatting state.
attributes.docstring_full: Fragment-level text formatting state. Wraps the underlying TextState on a TextFragment and exposes the additional fragment-level members (Font typed as Font, DrawTextRectangleBorder, TabStops, IsFitRectangle).

attributes.docstring: Copy every public formatting property from textState into this state.
Background fill applied behind the fragment text.
Character spacing (Tc) in text-space units.
Whether positioning treats Y as the baseline or the descender.
When true, a rectangular border is drawn around the text bounding box.
attributes.docstring_full: When true, a rectangular border is drawn around the text bounding box. Stored only — the renderer does not currently emit the border stroke.

attributes.docstring: The fragment's font: while the fragment's own face was never set, the one the caller set on every segment when they all name the same face; else the fragment's own.
External font data for embedding (set via FontRepository.OpenFont).
attributes.docstring_full: External font data for embedding (set via FontRepository.OpenFont). When set, TextBuilder will embed this font in the PDF instead of using Standard 14.

attributes.docstring: Gets or sets the name of the font family used for the text; null when not set.
The fragment's font size in points: while the fragment's own size was never set, the one the caller set on every segment when they all agree; else the fragment's own.
Font style flags (Bold / Italic).
Fill (non-stroking) colour applied to the rendered glyphs.
Text formatting options (wrap mode, line spacing mode, etc.).
Horizontal alignment of the fragment's text.
Horizontal scaling percentage (default 100).
Whether the text is rendered invisibly (rendering mode 3).
Whether the font is bold.
Returns true when the rendered text fits within the supplied rectangle at the current font / size.
Whether the font is italic.
Whether the text has strikethrough.
Whether the text is subscript.
Whether the text is superscript.
Whether the text is underlined.
Line spacing (leading) in text space units.
attributes.docstring_full: Line spacing (leading) in text space units. The line-box ascent this caller declares, in em (1 = the font size), or null to use the face's own. Only read under LineBox. A face carries several defensible ascent/descent pairs (AFM, hhea, OS/2 typo, win, the bounding box) and a typographic system picks one -- some scale the pair they pick. A caller that must match such a system declares the pair here instead of distorting the leading to compensate, which would move the pitch as well as the seat.

attributes.docstring: The line-box descent this caller declares, in em, as a POSITIVE distance below the baseline.
attributes.docstring_full: The line-box descent this caller declares, in em, as a POSITIVE distance below the baseline. Null uses the face's own. See LineBoxAscentEm.

attributes.docstring: Line spacing (leading) in text-space units.

attributes.docstring_full: Stroke line width (the w operator) in effect for the run: the pen a stroking RenderingMode outlines the glyphs with. An absorbed run reports the width that was set when it was shown; a run written by the generator carries the pen it was stroked with (a synthesised bold weight strokes with a size-proportional pen). 1.0 is the PDF default.

attributes.docstring: Measure the height of a single character at the current font / size, in points.
Measure the rendered width of str at the current font / size, in points.
Glyph rendering mode (fill / stroke / clip).
Rotation angle in degrees.
Whether the text has strikethrough.
Stroke (outline) colour.
Whether the text is subscript.
Whether the text is superscript.
Tab-stop settings inherited from the owning fragment.
String token inserted into the rendered text in place of a tab character.
attributes.docstring_full: String token inserted into the rendered text in place of a tab character. Returns "\t" — the default tab-character placeholder.

attributes.docstring: Wrap the fragment's underlying state so writes flow back to it.
Text height in points: (Ascent + |Descent|) · FontSize / 1000 from the font's descriptor metrics.
attributes.docstring_full: Text height in points: (Ascent + |Descent|) · FontSize / 1000 from the font's descriptor metrics. Falls back to the bare font size when no descriptor metrics are available.

attributes.docstring: Text rise (superscript/subscript offset).
On-page start X (points) of the text this state belongs to.
attributes.docstring_full: On-page start X (points) of the text this state belongs to. Populated for states surfaced through PhysicalSegment.

attributes.docstring: Whether the text is underlined.
Word spacing (Tw) in text-space units.
Base class for text-processing options.
Represents a text paragraph that can be placed on a page via AppendParagraph.
attributes.docstring_full: Represents a text paragraph that can be placed on a page via AppendParagraph. Lines are appended via AppendLine or AppendLine and rendered top-to-bottom within the Rectangle bounding box.

attributes.docstring: Append a text fragment as a new line in the paragraph.

Background colour painted behind the whole paragraph block: one rectangle the height of the block, as wide as the widest line plus BackgroundPad (or the content width when a line overflows), seated at the block's bottom-left.
attributes.docstring_full: Background colour painted behind the whole paragraph block: one rectangle the height of the block, as wide as the widest line plus BackgroundPad (or the content width when a line overflows), seated at the block's bottom-left. Null paints nothing.

attributes.docstring: Begin a batched edit window.
attributes.docstring_full: Begin a batched edit window. An attached paragraph is laid out once when appended and again only at save time if it changed, so there is no per-edit work to batch — kept for symmetry with the flush model.

attributes.docstring: End a batched edit window started by BeginEdit.

attributes.docstring_full: Line spacing (leading) in text space units. The line-box ascent this caller declares, in em (1 = the font size), or null to use the face's own. Only read under LineBox. A face carries several defensible ascent/descent pairs (AFM, hhea, OS/2 typo, win, the bounding box) and a typographic system picks one -- some scale the pair they pick. A caller that must match such a system declares the pair here instead of distorting the leading to compensate, which would move the pitch as well as the seat.

Walks the content stream tracking the CTM (q/Q/cm) and the paint colours; every sub-path that is actually painted (fill/stroke/fill-stroke) becomes one element. Clip-only paths (ending in n ) and text are ignored. The elements can be replayed onto another page with AddGraphics, and top-level elements can be moved (Position) or removed on their source page — edits rewrite only the elements' own operator ranges, so text and other non-vector content is untouched.

attributes.docstring_full: zlib (RFC 1950) deflating output stream — a public helper on the public API surface. Bytes written are zlib-compressed into the destination stream. Call Finish (or dispose) to flush the compression trailer; the destination stream is left open. The compression is the library's own deflater, so the bytes written are the same on every host and target framework.

zlib (RFC 1950) inflating input stream — a public helper on the public API surface.
attributes.docstring_full: zlib (RFC 1950) inflating input stream — a public helper on the public API surface. Reads zlib-compressed data from the source stream and yields the decompressed bytes. The source stream is left open. The decompression is the library's own inflater: the first read takes the rest of the source and inflates it; a seekable source is then left just past the compressed stream. A stream cut short yields what it holds; a malformed one yields the bytes before the fault and then throws InvalidDataException.
